chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Hurry to do four [good deeds] before four [things happen]: use your youth before your old age, your health before your illness, your wealth before your poverty, and your life before your death.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things one should utilize before they are lost, according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on proactive spiritual preparation (*istifrah*) by leveraging current blessings before their inevitable loss. It serves as a practical reminder to prioritize worship and good deeds during periods of ease, aligning with the concept of *falah* (success) through timely action.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-85 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Musa ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Qazvan, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Muslim al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq(MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“You should benefit from four things before four things happen: use your youth before you get old; use your health before you get ill; use your wealth before you get poor; and use your life before your death.”
